newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Sept palm oil shipment to Iraq to go ahead - FELDA.
newsitem.headline: Sept palm oil shipment to Iraq to go ahead - FELDA.

text.p: A shipment of Malaysian palm oil to Iraq for September delivery will go ahead as scheduled despite the U.S. missile attacks on the Gulf state, a Malaysian plantation official said on Thursday.
But further shipments for October to November delivery are still uncertain, a Federal Land Developement Authority (FELDA) official said.

"As far as I know, we are going ahead with the September shipment. About 13,000 to 15,000 tonnes of palm oil will be loaded into the vessel in the Malaysian east coast port of Kuantan sometime in the middle of the month," he said.
"But I am not sure whether there will be a delay from October to November."
The official added that even if there is a delay, it should not have much impact on the palm oil market as the amount bought by Iraq was small.
"We can still sell it off to other consumers," he said.
The official said he was uncertain of the total quantity of palm oil likely to go to Iraq, but added that it was "smaller" than the 80,000 tonnes reported in the market on Wednesday.

A report circulated that Iraq had bought about 80,000 tonnes of RBD palm oil two months ago for shipment between August to November. But talk that the Iraqi consignments might be delayed by the U.S. attack had no effect on Malaysian palm oil prices.
Traders said any delay in the shipments would not have any significant impact on domestic stock levels.
"If there is a delay in shipment, it will not make a great difference to our stock level," one dealer said, adding that exports for August were very good.
Malaysian traders are estimating end-August stocks at between 750,000-755,000 tonnes.
